title: ASIC sues ex-Super Retail boss Heraghty
full_text:
The corporate cop is suing former Super Retail Group boss Anthony Heraghty, alleging he breached his directors’ duties and misled his board and the market over an illicit workplace affair.
In civil proceedings filed in Federal Court on Monday, the Australian Securities & Investments Commission alleged Mr Heraghty failed to disclose and manage conflicts of interest arising from an undisclosed relationship he had with a senior executive at the company.
Super Retail, which owns chains Supercheap Auto, Rebel, BCF and Macpac, sacked Mr Heraghty in September 2025 after he failed to disclose to the board the true nature of his relationship with former head of HR Jane Kelly.
The sacking came after Super Retail racked up a $30m legal bill over the workplace scandal, including a multimillion-dollar settlement deal with two whistleblowers, who sued the retail group last year.
ASIC alleges Mr Heraghty’s actions exposed Super Retail to foreseeable risks of harm, including risks to its corporate reputation.
The former retail boss, who long denied the affair, continued to supervise Ms Kelly and participated in decisions affecting her employment, remuneration, incentives, rewards and redundancy package despite the conflict of interest, ASIC said.
He also participated in board and committee discussions of complaints and anticipated legal proceedings concerning the alleged undisclosed relationship; and provided or authorised information to be released to Super Retail’s board and the market that omitted information concerning the alleged undisclosed relationship and was therefore misleading, the regulator alleged.
The scandal erupted in 2024 when Super Retail former chief legal officer Rebecca Farrell and former company secretary Amelia Berczelly complained about a toxic work environment, including workplace bullying, and exposed the affair between Mr Heraghty and Ms Kelly.
Among the allegations levelled at the seasoned executive were that he misused company funds to carry on the alleged affair, as well as claims of harassment.
Court documents later claimed Mr Heraghty’s wife became aware of the relationship between the two executives in March 2023, when she accessed his phone and discovered the affair had, at that point, been ongoing for three years. Mr Heraghty and his wife have since divorced, while Ms Kelly left Super Retail in late 2023.
The company defended Mr Heraghty for more than a year Continued on Page 19 Continued from Page 13 amid the whistleblower claims of the undisclosed relationship, conducting its own review and investigation into the allegations and ultimately finding them to be unsubstantiated.
The ASX-listed retail group later sacked Mr Heraghty when the company uncovered more information about the affair, leading the board to conclude his story was “not satisfactory”.
The retail group settled a legal case with the two whistleblowers days later, for an undisclosed sum.
ASIC chair Sarah Court said Mr Heraghty put himself in a position where his personal interests conflicted with his duties to Super Retail and that he failed to properly disclose and manage that conflict.
“The allegations in this matter raise important issues about governance, transparency and trust in the information provided to boards and the market,” Ms Court said. “This case is not about private relationships, but whether a director properly disclosed and managed conflicts of interest and met their duties to the company and shareholders.
“Trust and integrity underpin Australia’s market and corporate sector, and it is critical that directors fully meet their obligations of transparency and accountability; where we consider they have failed to do so ASIC will not hesitate to act,” she said.
ASIC alleges Mr Heraghty’s actions exposed Super Retail to risks, including to its corporate reputation, complaints and litigation, regulatory action, costs, and harm to its share price and shareholders. The regulator is seeking declarations of contravention, pecuniary penalties and disqualification orders.
The lawsuit comes just a month after family-owned kitchen appliances and goods retailer Winning Group named Mr Heraghty as its new chief executive, amid talk it is preparing for an initial public offering next year. Investment firm Ellerston Capital is a key investor in Winning Group. Mr Heraghty and Ellerston Capital chief investment officer David Keelan were contacted for comment.
